findings.title: Update calendars using the booking organizer's credentials
findings.body: The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the caller and the caller's credentials. When the caller is not the booking organizer, those credentials do not authorize updates to the organizer's existing calendar event. Guests are already persisted before this update is attempted, so the booking can gain attendees while the actual calendar invitation remains unchanged or the mutation fails. Use the booking organizer's credentials for the calendar update.

findings.title: Authorize team administrators or owners rather than requiring both
findings.body: The isTeamAdminOrOwner check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. This requires the caller to satisfy both role checks instead of either one. A team administrator who is neither the organizer nor an attendee is consequently rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team booking. Combine the role checks with OR.

findings.title: Deduplicate incoming guests on the server
findings.body: uniqueGuests only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove repetitions within the submitted guests array. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct API request containing the same new address twice passes validation and sends both entries to createMany. This can create duplicate attendees and duplicate invitations despite the UI's uniqueness validation. Enforce uniqueness server-side before inserting attendees.

findings.title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without lowercasing them. Zod's email validation accepts uppercase characters, so submitting a mixed-case version of a blacklisted address bypasses the blacklist and receives an invitation. Normalize incoming addresses before applying the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.

findings.title: Respect event-type email suppression when adding guests
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee, unlike the adjacent scheduling and location-change flows that honor disableStandardEmails metadata. The handler also does not pass event-type metadata to this function. Adding a guest therefore sends standard emails even for event types whose host or attendee notifications have explicitly been disabled. Accept the metadata and apply the existing host and attendee suppression checks.

findings.title: Handle seated bookings through the seat allocation flow
findings.body: This mutation accepts seated bookings but inserts ordinary attendees without checking seatsPerTimeSlot or creating seat references. The new action is also exposed for these bookings. As a result, callers can add attendees beyond the configured capacity, and those attendees have no seat reference for the seat-specific cancellation and rescheduling links used by the booking UI. Either reject seated bookings in this flow or allocate guests through the seat-booking logic with capacity checks and seat references.

findings.title: Reject guest additions to inactive or unconfirmed bookings
findings.body: The handler checks permissions and guest addresses but never checks the booking status. An authorized caller can invoke it for a cancelled or rejected booking, after which new guests receive AttendeeScheduledEmail and existing attendees receive an ICS request marked CONFIRMED. Pending bookings can likewise receive confirmed invitations without being approved. Validate that the booking is in a supported status before inserting guests or issuing calendar updates and notifications.
